capabilities
capabilities · 5 records
  1. domain
    demand forecasting
    assessment
    Strong recent quarterly execution and conservative ranges; multiyear demand remains a judgment.
    confidence
    medium-high short term, medium long term
    evidence
    evidence · 2 records
    1. Eight consecutive reported quarters meet or exceed original USD revenue range; five above, three within.
    2. Management checks customers and their customers and now reports checking data-center build-outs/power.
    outcome
    Supports a strong near-term starting path, not automatic 25% growth from today.
    counterexamples
    counterexamples · 3 records
    1. Raising 2026 capex from $52-56bn to $60-64bn demonstrates forecast revision rather than perfect foresight.
    2. 2023 revenue declined in the historical record.
    3. Demand signals may overlap across customers; signed product plans are not end-user monetization.
    source Ids
    source Ids · 10 records
    1. TSM-2024Q4
    2. TSM-2025Q1
    3. TSM-2025Q2
    4. TSM-2025Q3
    5. TSM-2025Q4
    6. TSM-2026Q1
    7. TSM-2026Q2
    8. TSM-2026Q3
    9. TSM-2Q26-CALL
    10. TSM-3Q26-CALL
  2. domain
    product delivery
    assessment
    Leading-node ramp has revenue and yield evidence; future A14 remains a roadmap.
    confidence
    high recent, medium forward
    evidence
    evidence · 2 records
    1. N2 entered high-volume production Q4 2025 and accounts for 8% of Q3 2026 wafer revenue.
    2. 7nm-and-below is 79% of wafer revenue.
    outcome
    Demonstrated ability to monetize leading nodes, enabling measured persistence in margin/returns.
    counterexamples
    counterexamples · 2 records
    1. A14 2027 risk/2028 volume-production objectives are not realized.
    2. Node mix and competitor yield improvements can change advantage quickly.
    source Ids
    source Ids · 2 records
    1. TSM-3Q26-MR
    2. TSM-3Q26-CALL
  3. domain
    capacity execution
    assessment
    Operational ramp competence is visible, with larger overseas execution burden ahead.
    confidence
    medium-high
    evidence
    evidence · 2 records
    1. Arizona first fab high-volume production confirmed in Q4 2024.
    2. N2 now ramps across Hsinchu/Kaohsiung; capacity expected to more than double in 2027.
    outcome
    Capacity delivers current shipments, but almost 20 fab projects make forward workload unusually large.
    counterexamples
    counterexamples · 2 records
    1. Overseas dilution increases as several fabs open.
    2. Tool availability, power/water, skills, labor and subsidies can delay economically usable output.
    source Ids
    source Ids · 3 records
    1. TSM-4Q25-CALL
    2. TSM-3Q26-CALL
    3. TSM-FY25-IFRS
  4. domain
    cost control
    assessment
    Better utilization and productivity repeatedly beat margin guidance; FX and mix must be separated from skill.
    confidence
    medium-high
    evidence
    evidence · 2 records
    1. Q3 2026 58.7% EBIT margin versus 56-58% guide; Q2 60.3% versus 56.5-58.5%.
    2. Q3 gross margin fell 1.3 points as N2 ramp diluted margins, as directionally anticipated.
    outcome
    Justifies above-industry mature economics, with explicit fade for foreign-fab cost.
    counterexamples
    counterexamples · 2 records
    1. 2025Q3 favorable currency versus guide helped margins; not all beat is cost control.
    2. N2 and overseas costs can outlast productivity gains.
    source Ids
    source Ids · 5 records

    2. TSM-2026Q2
    3. TSM-2026Q3
    4. TSM-2Q26-CALL

  5. domain
    capital allocation
    assessment
    Investment has supported profitable growth, but new capex is a demanding long-duration commitment.
    confidence
    medium-high historical, medium forecast
    evidence
    evidence · 2 records
    1. FY2025 operating cash flow TWD2.275tr versus capex TWD1.272tr.
    2. Current balance sheet has substantial cash/investments; regular dividends.
    outcome
    Model requires reinvestment and returns decay; no valuation premium solely for leadership reputation.
    counterexamples
    counterexamples · 3 records
    1. Higher construction/tool cost per wafer and foreign fab economics may depress future incremental returns.
    2. Cash/ROE is not ROIC; refundable customer receipts and NCI/leases affect claims.
    3. Taiwan continuity risk is outside management control.

thesis
Leading nodes/packaging keep strong growth through A14 and overseas ramps; diversification costs and customer bargaining gradually reduce margins. Growth decelerates well below the recent AI ramp.

AI build-out slows while higher-cost fabs open, utilization falls, and customer pricing power grows. This is a continuing-business downside, not a Taiwan conflict/asset-loss scenario.

maturity Rationale
Five years model N2/A14 and current overseas build-out. Ten further years fade growth/returns through several node cycles; no flat 25% growth extension. Twenty years would give excessive unsupported competitive advantage.

classification
Mechanical consequence of explicit analytical scenario; not market calibrated, recommendation or verified equity value
maturity Revenue Unit
TWD millions
growth Currency Policy
Forecast nominal TWD revenue from TIFRS TTM. USD management guidance is a separate plausibility check; no mixing flow FX with spot equity FX. First-year next-12-month growth is not FY2027 over FY2026 calendar growth.
reinvestment Policy
Net reinvestment = positive incremental revenue / marginal sales-capital, with an 8%-of-revenue floor in the bear contraction year. D&A/NWC/capex are a consistency audit, not additional deductions. Marginal capital efficiency fades to ROIC/(margin*(1-tax)) by maturity, making terminal economics coherent.
capex Interpretation
First-year base implied gross capex is about one-third of revenue, close to the recent capital-spending scale. Capex and D&A depend on equipment timing; fixed replacement needs mean low-growth downside cannot assume cash liquidation of fab assets.
sbc Policy
Expense recurring compensation in EBIT; 0.05% of forecast revenue is an analytical reserve, slightly above FY2025 reported SBC intensity. Do not infer no dilution from low reported SBC.

invalidators
invalidators · 5 records
  1. Leading-node customer demand or effective utilization falls below capacity additions for multiple quarters.
  2. N2/A14 qualification, yields or packaging throughput miss customer production windows.
  3. Overseas ramp dilution materially exceeds 3-4 points, or tool/energy inflation outstrips strategic pricing.
  4. A few major customers reduce orders, insource a meaningful share, or shift to competing foundries.
  5. Export controls, power/water disruptions or Taiwan geopolitical events impair continuity; a normal WACC increment cannot fully represent asset-loss tail risk.

valuation Timing Policy
valuation Timing Policy · 3 fields
valuation Date
2026-10-17
operating Model Convention
end-of-year discounting from latest reported annual/TTM baseline; illustrative operating EV only
unresolved
Precise stub-period cash generation, distributions, new financings and post-balance-sheet claims must be rolled to valuation date before per-share release.
forecast Status
Independent analytical scenarios; all current and unresolved claims retained; no implementable equity recommendation or per-share output.
grant Treatment
Marginal sales/capital represents net economic reinvestment after ordinary support; no separate grant asset or cash grant added. Implied gross capex is an audit proxy before a detailed grants/accruals bridge, not a precise management capex reconstruction.
capitalization Policy
capitalization Policy · 4 fields
reported EBITBasis
Reported GAAP operating income for MU; TIFRS operating income for TSM. No synthetic starting-margin rewrite.
research And Development
Keep reported R&D expensed. No research-asset capitalization or amortization adjustment has been made. If a later model capitalizes R&D, it must restate both operating profit and invested capital consistently across history and forecast.
software And Leases
Maintain reported treatment in starting facts; detailed software/intangible additions and lease roll-forwards remain in final cash-flow reconciliation. Do not capitalize operating expenses merely to lift margins.
SBC
Recurring SBC remains an expense; no add-back that ignores dilution.
maintenance And Capital Path
maintenance And Capital Path · 7 fields
maintenance Definition
Economic replacement and technology-refresh spend is not separately reported. D&A is an audit proxy, not evidence that economic maintenance equals accounting depreciation.
early Years
MU direct gross capex/grants/D&A/NWC in years1–5; TSM net reinvestment with implied capex/D&A audit. Fixed commitments and technology refresh remain during downside.
later DARevenue Ratio
0.2
later Grants
MU cash-grant forecast ends after year5; TSM ordinary support embedded in net capital-efficiency judgment, with no extra asset.

stress Test

currency Consistency Choice
currency Consistency Choice · 6 fields
method
Nominal native-TWD cash flows and terminal growth discounted at nominal TWD WACC.
formula

limitation
Long-run Fisher/relative-inflation consistency assumption, not an empirically estimated FX path or observed TWD market rate. Risk allowances are analytical judgments. Current USD spot conversion remains a separate gate.
implementation Gate
Do not substitute USD WACC for TWD WACC; any implementation must preserve this explicit native-currency method or independently rebuild USD cash flows with an explicit FX path.
